answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns. Courtship rounds have no player turns, service rotation, Servants’ Hall use, or monument income; only the courtship event occurs.
answers.evidence: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters; resolve the round event, then ongoing effects; choose an activity tile; play exactly the required gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative ones; optionally buy one Market or Reserve tile; cleanup by sending used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and returning the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker. Events occur after rotation and before ongoing effects.
answers.evidence: ‘resolve the round event first. Then resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects’; ‘all servants used … go to Expended Service; all played gentry … personal discard pile’

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; round event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, so 6.1 qualifies the PR6 tile and guests for this activity even if four Service Help actions reduce current reputation to 3.4. Each action moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; none can be taken directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: ‘That level must meet or exceed the PR … It remains the screening level for the whole activity’; Service Help: ‘Lose 3 increments; move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service’

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours, choosing order within those groups. You cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid its loss at minimum; losses cannot go below 1.1. A guest with a money penalty requires the full payment. Positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money may fund it; if short, borrow if possible, and if still unable to pay, you cannot play that guest.
answers.evidence: ‘Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours’; ‘A money penalty must be fully payable’

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments for £100 and is repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant moved from Quarters to Available and is repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and is limited to once per turn as a special action. At 1.1 you cannot take special actions. Service Help cannot move a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special-action table lists the three costs and limits; ‘At minimum you cannot … take a special action’; Service Help ‘cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.’

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two non-underbutler servants from Servants for Hire into Expended Service, with no hiring fee. On upgrade, instead of that option you may recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: ‘Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service’; upgraded room ‘recruit one common servant … from any location on one opponent’s family board’

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman substitutes for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant even while that servant type is available.
answers.evidence: ‘Housekeeper … may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available’; ‘underbutler may substitute for any base male servant … even when that type remains available.’

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it goes from supply directly to Expended Service. Ordinarily it reaches Quarters at your next rotation and Available Service at your second subsequent rotation, though passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available sooner, and once in Quarters the listed effects can enable earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: ‘Butler’s Pantry … only way to acquire an underbutler’; ‘not immediately available’; ‘An opponent can never recruit your underbutler’

answers.answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot fall below £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing; PR limits play, not acquisition.
answers.evidence: ‘Pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300’; ‘Never acquire a duplicate’; ‘reputation does not restrict purchasing.’

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn. Reserve-eligible tiles go directly to Reserve and are replaced by another draw. If multiple spaces need filling, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Taking one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so there is no refill.
answers.evidence: ‘if a Market space became empty, slide remaining tiles left’; ‘Buying only one tile from a two-tile stack leaves an occupied space and causes no refill.’

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: ‘After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar’; ‘After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles’; full refresh occurs after ‘each of the first three courtships.’

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships 1–3, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Each player sums printed VP of tiles in the current theme’s face-up category, including negative tile VP; only a hybrid’s face-up category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. On a tie for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one objective; simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the objective deck’s bottom. Then open the relevant Reserve, refresh the Market, reveal the next theme while keeping earlier revealed themes, pass first player anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship steps specify Fairchild return, theme score, tie award and objective discard; upkeep says ‘pass first-player marker anticlockwise.’

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds and score tile VP for all four revealed themes; a category appearing twice counts twice, including negative VP. Highest score gets a VP card and Fairchild. Ties are broken by reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players may use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before moving to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: ‘total tile VP for all four revealed theme cards’; ‘Then players have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for their benefits where possible.’

answers.answer: End-game categories are improvement tiles (including negative VP), gentry in hand and discard (including negatives, family, and retained final Fairchild), fulfilled objectives, reputation, servants, wealth, and retained VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Wealth scores 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Highest total wins; ties go to the player with final Fairchild, then highest reputation level; if still tied, players share victory. Wheel position does not break ties.
answers.evidence: Final VP table lists all sources and reputation values; ‘Ties: tied player with final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied share victory.’

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup and two at round 6. Discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase retained final count without an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together before putting them face down on the objective deck’s bottom. Tile objectives require owning the tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: ‘Normally receive five at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score’; tile objectives require owning, ‘not upgrading.’

answers.answer: A VP-card benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP at game end; a card cannot provide both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: ‘You may use it immediately on drawing it, at any time on your own later turn … and once more after final courtship’; used cards go to ‘bottom of the VP deck.’

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined icon showing and flips after every use. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite each host once, upgrade into ongoing monuments, and never host again; their monument benefit starts on later turns. For a hybrid, only the currently face-up category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: ‘Normal activity tiles must upgrade after first use’; hybrids ‘flip after every use’; suites ‘upgrade into a monument’ and ‘can never host again.’

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve during ongoing effects on hosting turns and passes, after the round event; monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn, with no courtship income. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; the servant goes to Expended at turn end. You cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments give reputation ‘per ordinary turn … hosting or passing’; Servants’ Hall uses ‘any one available servant’; ‘Do not target a player at minimum reputation.’

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one casual guest from hand, a footman on the tile, and the guest’s normal service; it doubles all that guest’s favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity. Queen’s Suite uses one prestige guest from hand, a housekeeper on the tile, and the guest’s normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve the others normally, then it becomes a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler on the tile and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend without personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, not negative ones, keep the guest, and put it in discard at cleanup; it becomes a monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite comparison table; ‘All three suites have a fixed count of one guest; no effect may increase or decrease it.’

answers.answer: Give the first-player marker to a random player. Starting with that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Give a random player the first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise’; family bonus list names all four.

answers.answer: Set the common reputation-wheel baseline to level 1, position 1; after bonuses, Cavendish starts at 1.4 and the other families at 1.1. Stack 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Each player gets a butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter side showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady family cards. Ponsonby alone starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5 specify counters, starting reputation, servants, tiles, family cards and family bonus money.

answers.answer: For three players, put three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers in Servants for Hire. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and are unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: ‘one valet and one lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers’; unused servants ‘unavailable this game.’

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from the casual deck and deal two to each player’s hand; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules, not a separate play-time guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck’; starter guests ‘otherwise follow normal casual rules.’

answers.answer: For four players select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze are the two Estate monuments; choose at most one of them. Put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the bag. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments still go in the bag and do not count toward the setup selection.
answers.evidence: ‘one double-sided monument per player plus one, choosing at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze’; upgrade-into-monument tiles ‘always go in the bag and do not count.’

answers.answer: Fill six different Market spaces with eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside until the Market is filled, then return them to the bag. Stack eligible duplicates in the same space. Normal tiles show the upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids show the underlined hybrid icon. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number starting at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments cannot enter.
answers.evidence: Opening Market: ‘six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less … not Servants’ Hall, and not a double-sided monument.’

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, marker at round 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme for open courtship and keep revealed themes in order. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. Thus the first theme is open, and older revealed themes remain in play.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle theme and VP decks separately. Reveal the first theme (open courtship); keep revealed themes in order through the game’; Fairchilds face up.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters first moves to Available Service; the servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each advances one space only. An available servant not used remains available.
answers.evidence: ‘move servants in Servants’ Quarters to Available Service first, then those in Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters’; ‘Unused available servants remain available.’

answers.answer: No immediate Fair reward if the Private Study is not upgraded when the round event resolves; upgrading it later in that turn does not change that check. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9, without needing to host it.
answers.evidence: Village Fair: ‘If your Private Study is already upgraded, immediately gain £300 and 2 reputation. No reward if it is not upgraded at this step.’

answers.answer: The event resolves after service rotation and before ongoing effects on a hosting turn, or after servants and discarded gentry return and before ongoing effects on a pass. At round 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret. Passing players also resolve the event at that position in the turn order.
answers.evidence: Round-track events are resolved before ongoing effects; ‘Draw Objectives … Draw two objectives; keep both secret’; passing uses the same event order.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on tiles and guests while hosting. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts and types.
answers.evidence: National Holiday: ‘Ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting; still obey all other requirements, including service and gentry counts/types.’

answers.answer: Yes. Builders’ Holiday allows any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling; each tile keeps the space or Reserve price plus modifier that applied before the sequence. Do not refresh between purchases with a special action or VP card. The same unchanged-market and no-refresh restriction applies to Market Purchase VP-card benefits; refill resulting empty spaces together afterward.
answers.evidence: ‘finish all purchases before sliding/refilling’; ‘single-unchanged-market restriction, including no refresh between purchases, applies to both Builders’ Holiday and a Market Purchase VP-card benefit.’

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; leave the Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside Market tiles to the bag and mix them in. Reserve tiles remain as they were.
answers.evidence: ‘set all Market tiles aside … leave the Reserve unchanged … then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix.’

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Moving clockwise past position 5 to 1 raises a level; moving anticlockwise past 1 to 5 lowers a level; each level spans five increments. Standard range is 1.1 to 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond 1.1. At Max.5, spend excess immediately on special actions if desired, otherwise it is lost.
answers.evidence: Reputation rules specify increments, boundary crossings, ‘Minimum is 1.1, maximum … 7.5 (Max.5)’ and excess at Max.5 is lost unless spent immediately.

answers.answer: Money is public, players may not give or receive money between them, and you may never spend more than you have. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if it runs out.
answers.evidence: ‘Money held is public’; ‘may not give or receive money between players’; ‘Money supply is unlimited.’

answers.answer: Family members can fill ladies or gentlemen requirements according to gender, but casual-guest requirements require casual guests and exclude family. Play exactly the printed number and types; no extras. Family has no PR and needs no personal service.
answers.evidence: Ladies/gentlemen include female/male family; casual/prestige requirements ‘exclude family’; ‘You cannot exceed or fall short’; family has no PR and no personal service.

answers.answer: An ordinary guest-invite favour draws the indicated guest from its deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to your hand. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of that guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Ordinary invite: ‘Draw … reveal … add it to hand’; screened draws reveal only kept cards and rejected cards go to the bottom unrevealed.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss anyone. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put a dismissed guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: ‘Dismissal is always optional’; eligible guest may come from ‘hand, current activity or discard’; dismissed guest ‘is no longer yours.’

answers.answer: Lord: gain £200. Lady: choose to screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: gain both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table lists Lord, Lady, Heir and Asquith Dowager effects.

answers.answer: The Young Lady’s bonus applies only with a male prestige guest attending: not a male casual guest, and not a female prestige guest; Charles Fairchild does trigger it because he is a male prestige guest. The bonus is two reputation. She still draws one casual guest in every case.
answers.evidence: Young Lady: ‘Draw one casual guest; additionally gain two reputation if a male prestige guest attends’; Charles is stated to trigger the bonus.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither is family: both may be dismissed under the normal guest rule and have no family dismissal immunity.
answers.evidence: Fairchilds are ‘prestige guests with no PR’; Charles requires valet and gives three reputation; Elizabeth requires lady’s maid and gives both listed favours; neither has family dismissal immunity.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. A player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: ‘Miss Elizabeth Perkins (reduce one opponent by one reputation) and Miss Florence Oliver (reduce one opponent by two, and lose one yourself); minimum-reputation protection still applies.’

answers.answer: The Barn gives one reputation whenever you host an Estate activity. It gives no reputation just for owning an Estate tile or when passing.
answers.evidence: ‘every time you host an Estate activity, gain one reputation. It gives no reputation just for owning an Estate tile or passing.’

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments to move one Quarters servant to Available and cannot take directly from Expended. The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, each ordinary turn without reputation cost; send that used servant to Expended at turn end.
answers.evidence: Service mechanism table gives all three mechanisms; Quarters tile permits ‘one servant still in … Quarters’ and used servant goes to Expended.

answers.answer: The front-side Private Study activity requires a butler and two family, and has no tile favour. It upgrades into an ongoing tile, so you cannot host it repeatedly; its upgraded effect gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds only, without staffing or hosting it again.
answers.evidence: ‘Private Study hosts two family with a butler, has no tile favour, then upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile’; Village Fair effect is specified.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded, it uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring.
answers.evidence: ‘Main Library: unupgraded activity uses a butler and two family to draw one extra objective; after upgrading it uses a butler and three family to draw one VP card’; extra objectives increase final retained count.

answers.answer: The Objective VP-card benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Objective benefit: ‘Draw two objectives, keep one, return the other to bottom … This gives one additional retained objective.’

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants, including those in Expended Service, directly to Available Service for immediate use. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Refresh Service: ‘Move all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended Service; usable immediately’; Service Help comparison follows.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, not an underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot provide service immediately while in Expended Service; it must first become available through service movement or an applicable recovery effect.
answers.evidence: Hire Servant: ‘Take one servant from Servants for Hire, not underbutler, into Expended Service’; service is supplied by available servants, with Quarters tile exception.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest can return one gentry, including a family member, from your personal discard to hand. If used before Invite Gentry, you may then play that returned card as an attendee this turn, subject to normal requirements; returning it does not automatically make it attend.
answers.evidence: Refresh Guest: ‘including a family member from personal discard to hand’; before Invite Gentry, ‘you may choose that returned card to attend.’

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids; it excludes butlers, housekeepers and underbutlers. Ordinary service VP gives 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Basic-servant objective ‘only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids’; ordinary servant VP is ‘2 VP for every servant’; objective gives 7 VP for ten total.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite counts as an Estate tile and a monument; upgraded Lionheart Suite counts as a Prestige tile and a monument. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Monuments retain their tile category and count for both monument and category objectives; Queen’s Suite and Lionheart examples are explicit; hybrids use face-up category.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. The required tiles need only be owned at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Objective list names Nature Group (11 VP) and Domestic Group (12 VP); owning tiles suffices, ‘using or upgrading them is unnecessary.’

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective counts prestige guests; the every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests. A Fairchild retained from final courtship is a prestige guest and counts as a guest. Only each complete group of three scores; an incomplete remainder scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Guest bonuses: ‘1 VP per prestige guest; or 1 VP per complete three guests (all nonfamily guests)’; prestige guests include a final Fairchild.

answers.answer: The base reputation objective awards 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or break reputation ties; reputation VP and ties use level.
answers.evidence: Reputation objective: maximum level (7), regardless of wheel position; wealth objective: at least £1200; final VP and tie rules use level and ignore position.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require a butler and exactly three family cards. The unupgraded tile draws one prestige guest. The upgraded tile draws one prestige guest and may dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace: both sides require ‘one butler and exactly three family’; front draws prestige guest; upgraded draws one and optionally dismisses; ‘never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.’

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in your personal discard still belong to you and score normally unless dismissed.
answers.evidence: ‘There is no hand or discard-pile limit’; ‘discard-pile gentry score normally.’

answers.answer: The Reserve is public; you may inspect all its tiles at any time and buy any one, including one under another tile in a stack. There is no top-tile-only restriction.
answers.evidence: ‘Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection. You may inspect all tiles at any time and buy any one … including a tile underneath another in a stack.’

answers.answer: No. You may choose to pass. If the preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; you cannot exceed or fall short of its printed gentry requirement. If no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: ‘Without all required gentry and service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.’

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you can use the free Market refresh benefit, one paid special-action Refresh Market, and multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action refresh; pass and VP refreshes have separate availability.
answers.evidence: ‘You may combine those cards with one free passing-benefit refresh and one paid special-action refresh’; other refresh methods do not use the special action allowance.

answers.answer: No; special actions are available only on your own turn, not as interrupts during another player’s turn. On your own turn, hosting or passing, you may take them at any time with sufficient reputation, including before or during a reputation favour.
answers.evidence: ‘Special actions are available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing’; special actions may be taken ‘before or even in the middle of resolving a reputation favour.’

answers.answer: No. Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional, so you must take an ordinary printed guest invite while resolving the other favours. An optional dismissal may be declined; if taken, you choose an eligible guest to put on the bottom of its matching deck.
answers.evidence: ‘Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional (such as “may” or guest dismissal)’; dismissal is ‘always optional.’
